beats.narration_text: Research Computing on Explorer and AICR. Logging into AICR with Claude. How to let Claude Code log into the AICR cluster for you and run commands there, while your key and your passphrase never leave your hands.

shot.visual_intent: Film identity and short teaching description, visible immediately; Liam speaks playlist, title, summary

beats.narration_text: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. First, a correction. To let Claude log into AICR, the shared GPU cluster, you do not hand it your password. AICR has no password. You unlock a key once, yourself, and Claude never sees it.

beats.narration_text: Six terms. A private key: a secret file that proves who you are. A certificate: a signed note from AICR saying that key is yours. A passphrase: the password that locks the key file. The ssh-agent: a helper that holds your unlocked key in memory. BatchMode: a setting that makes ssh refuse to ask any question. And a login node: the shared computer you land on when you log in.

beats.narration_text: AICR has no password. At the front door it checks two things. A private key, a secret file that only you hold. And a certificate, a note that AICR's own certificate authority signed, saying that key is yours.

beats.narration_text: The key files come from one place: the AICR OnDemand portal, at o o d dot aicr dot AI. You sign in there with your institutional credentials. That step is yours, not Claude's.

beats.narration_text: Download the folder called aicr keys. Inside are four files. Your private key, locked with a passphrase. Its public half. Your certificate, which is the credential. And a file holding your first passphrase.

beats.narration_text: Put the files in your dot ssh folder, set their permissions, and swap the first passphrase for one only you know. Windows is the same, in PowerShell. Then delete the downloaded passphrase file.

beats.narration_text: Now the problem. Claude Code runs commands with no keyboard attached. If ssh stops to ask for the passphrase, nobody can answer, and the command hangs or fails.

beats.narration_text: The fix is not to give Claude the passphrase. The fix is to unlock the key before Claude arrives, once, in your own terminal, into a helper called ssh-agent. The agent holds the unlocked key in memory.

beats.narration_text: From then on, when ssh needs the key, it asks the agent, and the agent answers. The key never leaves the agent. Claude does the work. The secret never passes through it.

beats.narration_text: Add one block to your ssh config. Host aicr gives the cluster a short name. Then its host name, your AICR user name, your key file, and your certificate file.

beats.narration_text: Identities only offers just this key. Server alive interval stops idle connections dropping. Add keys to agent loads the key into the agent on first use. Use keychain is for macOS only, and ignore unknown makes other systems skip it.

beats.act: IV · Rules For A Shared Cluster
beats.narration_text: When you ask, Claude runs one ssh command with BatchMode on, followed by your read-only commands. Claude Code asks you to approve it. On a shared system, approve each ssh command, at least the first few times.

beats.act: IV · Rules For A Shared Cluster
beats.narration_text: Rule one. Read only first. Look before you change anything: s info, s queue for your own jobs, s acct, job stats, ls, and module avail.

shot.visual_intent: Six command pills in mono land one by one on a row under an eye drawing: sinfo, squeue -u $USER, sacct, jobstats, ls, module avail; each takes a check; the heading 'Read only first' stays above.

beats.act: IV · Rules For A Shared Cluster
beats.narration_text: Rule two. Never compute on a login node. Login nodes are shared, capped at four CPU cores and eight gigabytes of memory per user. Heavy work goes through Slurm, the scheduler: s batch, or s alloc and s run for a live session.

shot.visual_intent: The small login-node rack with a meter capped at '4 cores' and '8 GB'; a heavy job box tries to run there and is stopped at the cap; it is redirected to a 'Slurm' queue gate and on to the big AICR rack.

beats.narration_text: The error you will see most is permission denied, public key. It usually means one of three things. The key is not unlocked, by far the most common after a reboot. Or the certificate is expired or missing. Or the key's permissions are wrong.

shot.visual_intent: A white plaque with 'Permission denied (publickey)' in mono; three cause cards fan out beneath it: 'Key not unlocked' (largest, most common), 'Certificate expired or missing', 'Wrong permissions'.
shot.motion_claim: A white plaque with 'Permission denied (publickey)' in mono; three cause cards fan out beneath it: 'Key not unlocked' (largest, most common), 'Certificate expired or missing', 'Wrong permissions'.

beats.narration_text: Here is the trap. An empty agent looks exactly like an expired certificate. The error is the same. So check the agent with S S H add dash l before you blame the certificate.

shot.visual_intent: Two identical error plaques side by side; behind the left one an empty agent, behind the right an expired certificate, both hidden by a curtain; the command pill 'ssh-add -l' sweeps across and lifts the left curtain: the agent is empty.

beats.narration_text: Then, if the agent holds the key, check the certificate: is it still valid? If it is not, renew it in OnDemand. And set the private key's permissions to six hundred.

beats.narration_text: Bad configuration option: add ignore unknown above the keychain line. Connection timed out: try another network, because AICR needs no VPN. Drops when idle: server alive interval sixty. Empty after a restart: S S H add again, on a Mac with the keychain flag.

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. AICR checks a key and a certificate, not a password. Claude cannot type a passphrase, so you unlock the key once into the ssh-agent. Test with BatchMode: even an emptied agent logged in on a Mac. Claude runs read-only commands, and asks before it changes anything. The key and the passphrase never go into a prompt. And when you see permission denied, check the agent before you blame the certificate.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: Log into the AICR cluster with ssh aicr and run read-only commands only. Run: whoami, hostname, pwd, s info with its output format set to percent fourteen P, percent eleven l, percent six D, and s queue for my own user. Tell me the user name, the host, and which partitions exist. Do not submit, cancel or change anything, and do not run computation on the login node. Then check two things yourself. Did Claude run only read-only commands? And did it ever ask for, or print, your passphrase or your key?

props.command: Log into the AICR cluster with `ssh aicr` and run read-only commands only. Run: whoami, hostname, pwd, sinfo -o "%14P %11l %6D", squeue -u $USER. Tell me the user name, the host, and which partitions exist. Do not submit, cancel or change anything, and do not run computation on the login node.
output: Check: did Claude run only read-only commands, nothing that submits or changes?
Check: did Claude ever ask for, or print, your passphrase or key? It should not.
